paper_metadata.title: QUANTUM RESERVOIR COMPUTING FOR CREDIT CARD DEFAULT PREDICTION ON A NEUTRAL ATOM PLATFORM

experiments.description: Hybrid quantum-classical credit card default prediction using Quantum Reservoir Computing (QRC) on QuEra Aquila with detuning encoding, evaluated on the cleaned CARDS_30000 dataset in noiseless classical emulation and compared against classical baselines.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Reservoir Computing with local detuning encoding

hyperparameters.shots_for_feature_estimation: statevector and shot-based measurements evaluated; plateau reached at a few hundred shots

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 12 preprocessed features are mapped to local detuning amplitudes on a 12-qubit atom array; output features are expectation values of Zi and ZiZj over 5 timesteps.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Binary classification of whether a credit card client defaults in the following month.

problem_instance.description: Credit card default prediction on a public benchmark dataset from Taiwan.
problem_instance.dataset_name: Default of Credit Card Clients / CARDS_30000

dataset_specification.description: UCI dataset; original 30,000 samples cleaned to 29,601; 23 original features expanded to 24 after one-hot encoding SEX and MARRIAGE; PCA retained 11 PCs; hierarchical clustering aggregated features into 12 groups; train/validation/test split reported in appendix with test=4441 and validation=4440 for CARDS_30000.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Data cleaning removed samples with undocumented MARRIAGE and EDUCATION values; payment history values adjusted; absolute value scaling to [-1,1]; SEX and MARRIAGE one-hot encoded; EDUCATION kept numerical; PCA used to retain 11 PCs; agglomerative clustering in PCA space formed 12 feature clusters; cluster features averaged.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Validation-set F1-score used for hyperparameter selection; test-set evaluation reported; emulation on CARDS_30000 used to benchmark against DNN and classical reservoir/classical preprocessing baselines.

noise_model.noise_type: shot noise evaluated separately; this experiment refers to noiseless statevector emulation

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Data cleaning, absolute value scaling, one-hot encoding for SEX and MARRIAGE, PCA, agglomerative clustering, feature averaging.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Classifiers trained on QRC output features; resampling methods considered: None, SMOTE, K-SMOTE, Cluster Centroids; classifiers include KNN, SGD, Naïve Bayes, Logistic Model, Perceptron, SVM.

speedup_claims.conditions: SGD classifier on QRC output features versus DNN training on original 12 features
speedup_claims.caveats: Claimed in text as one order of magnitude shorter for SGD; exact ratio depends on resampling method.

speedup_claims.conditions: KNN, Naïve Bayes, Logistic Model, and Perceptron training on QRC output features versus DNN
speedup_claims.caveats: Text states two orders of magnitude shorter for these classifiers; based on Table 2 timings.

experiments.description: Hybrid quantum-classical credit card default prediction using Quantum Reservoir Computing with position encoding on QuEra Aquila, evaluated on the cleaned CARDS_1000 dataset with real hardware and compared to emulation and classical baselines.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Reservoir Computing with position encoding

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 12 preprocessed features are encoded into inter-atomic distances; position encoding requires 13 qubits for 12 features, with one extra atom and fixed global detuning.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Binary classification of whether a credit card client defaults in the following month.

problem_instance.description: Credit card default prediction on a public benchmark dataset, evaluated on the smaller CARDS_1000 subset for real-hardware testing.
problem_instance.dataset_name: Default of Credit Card Clients / CARDS_1000

dataset_specification.description: Nested stratified subset of CARDS_30000; CARDS_1000 contains 1000 samples; used to compare position and detuning encodings on Aquila; validation/test sizes reported in appendix as 150 each for CARDS_1000.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Same preprocessing as CARDS_30000: cleaning, scaling, one-hot encoding of SEX and MARRIAGE, PCA to 11 PCs, agglomerative clustering into 12 feature groups, averaging within clusters.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: F1-score on validation/test; real-hardware Aquila results compared against statevector and shot-based emulation; multiple resampling strategies evaluated.

noise_model.noise_type: hardware noise, shot noise, decoherence, and atom-position fluctuations
noise_model.mitigation_details: Correlation analysis over up to 1000 measurements per timestep on 10 random samples; selected nopt=240 total measurement samples, corresponding to 40 shots per timestep per sample.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Data cleaning, absolute value scaling, one-hot encoding for SEX and MARRIAGE, PCA, agglomerative clustering, feature averaging, embedding into a 2D Aquila register with 6 replicas separated by 15 µm.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Classifiers trained on QRC output features; resampling methods: None, SMOTE, K-SMOTE, Cluster Centroids; classifiers: KNN, SGD, Naïve Bayes, Logistic Model, Perceptron, SVM.

speedup_claims.caveats: No explicit speedup claim reported for this experiment.
